open_points.subject: Project-overview failure boundary
open_points.text: “the project overview answers a failed part as `temporarily_unavailable` with no value” does not define which post-authorization failures count as a failed part, especially a persistence failure while opening or using a transaction shared by multiple parts; elsewhere the same convention maps persistence failures to 500.
open_points.question: Which failures after the overview guard are converted into one or more `temporarily_unavailable` parts, and which still fail the whole overview with the ordinary error mapping?
options: Every post-guard Registry or persistence failure attributable to a component becomes `temporarily_unavailable`; only guard and request failures fail the operation.

Only dependency failures explicitly caught inside an individual component become `temporarily_unavailable`; transaction-opening, shared persistence, invariant, and unexpected failures fail the whole operation.
All post-guard read failures, including shared transaction failures, return a successful overview with every affected part unavailable.
open_points.default_guess: Convert expected Registry and persistence read failures that can be attributed to a component; return 500 for a failure before any component can be identified or for an unexpected invariant/programming failure.

witness.initial: A staff member is authorized to read an active project, and the project has an active budget.
events: The staff member requests the project overview.
The authorization guard and Registry lifecycle validation succeed.
The overview's first portal transaction cannot be opened, or raises PersistenceError before a component read identifies the affected part.
outcomes: The route returns 500 because the persistence failure is not attributable to a particular overview part.
The route returns a successful ProjectOverview with all portal-backed parts, or the first intended part, marked `temporarily_unavailable`.
witness.observer: The staff API caller sees either an HTTP failure or a successful partial overview.

open_points.subject: Availability propagation across dependent overview parts
open_points.text: “the project overview answers a failed part as `temporarily_unavailable` with no value” and “Each of the six parts gets its own availability” do not say how failure propagates when one read dependency supplies several parts.
open_points.question: When a dependency needed by multiple overview components fails, exactly which availability/value pairs become `temporarily_unavailable`, and may unaffected components still be returned?
options: Mark every component whose required inputs depend on the failed read unavailable, while returning components whose complete inputs were obtained.
Mark only the component whose builder encountered the failure; other builders retry or read independently.
Treat a shared-dependency failure as failure of the whole overview.
open_points.default_guess: Mark every transitively dependent component unavailable and return only components whose complete required inputs were obtained independently.

witness.initial: An active project has a budget, included expense allocations, progress records and payments; BudgetView needs expense allocations for actual-material totals, and PaymentSummaryView needs completed-work data derived from budget and progress.
events: An authorized viewer requests the overview.
The expense repository fails while the overview is composing its parts, while the budget, progress and payment repositories remain readable.
outcomes: Only `expenses` is `temporarily_unavailable`; the other parts are returned after independent reads.
Both `expenses` and every component requiring expense-derived values, including `budget`, are `temporarily_unavailable`, while independent parts remain available.
witness.observer: The viewer sees different availability flags and a different set of returned overview values.
